coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 45–50 min Z2 shakeout, 4–6 miles, sub-140 avg HR. You're 14 days out and your resting HR dropped to 53—you're primed. This is a pre-long-run primer: activate the aerobic system, clear metabolic junk, stay loose. Friday in taper means no intensity. Keep it conversational. Hills optional but not necessary; flat or rolling is fine. This run should feel like you're not even training.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Eat normal breakfast (carbs + protein) pre-run; you don't need a gel for 50 min easy. Post-run: 30–40g carbs + 15–20g protein within 30 min—chocolate milk, toast + egg, yogurt with granola. Your 10-hour sleep night shows you're recovering well; don't under-fuel in taper or you'll blunt adaptation. Hydrate consistently today; Alpine temps in September run cool, but you'll still lose 400–600ml per hour on Saturday's long run, so prepare your gut now.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your recovery score is 99 and resting HR is excellent—you've earned this. Sleep remains your main lever: tonight target 8–9 hours again. No foam rolling or aggressive mobility needed; gentle 10-min yoga or walk if restless. Hydrate 16–20oz fluid this evening. Tomorrow's long run is the main event; treat today as active prep, not as a day to squeeze out more fitness. Your nervous system is primed; don't waste it on junk miles.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: 14 days to race. You're in the zone: fitness is locked in, taper restlessness is normal. Today's easy run and tomorrow's long run are your last two chances to dial in race fueling, pacing feel, and mental anchors for the alpine terrain. Use these runs to rehearse: start conservative, settle into Z2–Z3 on climb, practice your aid-station rhythm. The Julian Alps will demand patience and presence—these final two runs are your dress rehearsal, not your last chance to get fit.
